newsitem.title: USA: Muni groups keep de minimis rule campaign going.
newsitem.headline: Muni groups keep de minimis rule campaign going.

text.p: Twenty-two municipal groups warned President Clinton on Wednesday that the U.S. House's proposed scale-back of the so-called de minimis rule will hurt the nation's schools.

The two-page letter to Clinton, who backs an all-out repeal of the de minimis rule, comes as congressional leaders prepare to meet later this week to reconcile differences in House and Senate tax bills.

The House voted last month to cut back the de minimis exemption for corporate holdings of munis to a flat $1 million, which muni lobbyists said would vitually gut the provision's usefulness for the muni market.
The Senate's bill does not include the repeal provision, notes the letter, spearheaded by the Government Finance Officers Association.

"This provision will simply shift the tax burden from the federal government to state and local governments," groups warned. They said, in particular, education and school construction - two Clinton priorities - will be "adversely affected" by a de minimis repeal.
"Many school districts lease various types of equipment including portable classrooms, telecommuncations systems, computers, software and school buses," groups said.

"This form of financing is particularly useful to school districts that cannot afford to borrow in the bond market, or do not have access to the bond market because of market inexperience or lack of credit rating agencies," groups said.
GFOA said it is gearing up to make a "major push" on Capitol Hill to keep de minimis repeal out of the final version of the tax bill.
Signers also include the National Association of State Treasurers, National League of Cities, U.S. Conference of Mayors, American Public Power Association, and others.
